runs.text: 1. What is the purpose of a looping control construct in Java?
A looping control construct is used when a statement or a block of statements needs to be executed multiple times.
Instead of writing the same statement repeatedly, we write it once inside a loop and allow the loop to execute it multiple times. This helps reduce code redundancy.
Code redundancy means writing the same statement or set of statements repeatedly when the same operation can be performed using a more efficient approach.
For example, if the same statement is written five times to print the same message, the code contains redundancy.
A loop can be used to write the statement once and execute it five times.
3. Why should code redundancy be avoided?
Code redundancy should be avoided because the same code does not need to be written repeatedly.
Instead, the redundant code can be identified, written only once, and executed multiple times using a looping control construct.
